description: The pie chart, titled in the context of “Narrative Media Framing in Political Discourse,” visually represents the proportional distribution of media bias across four political categories, based on a total sample of 100 units. The largest segment, colored blue, corresponds to “Right bias,” accounting for 30.0% (30 units). The second largest, in orange, is “Left bias” at 28.0% (28 units). The green segment, labeled “Left center bias,” represents 22.0% (22 units), while the smallest red segment, also labeled “Left center bias,” accounts for 20.0% (20 units). Each slice is clearly labeled with its category name, percentage, and raw count, and the segments are arranged in descending order clockwise from the top. A gray bar appears below the chart, though it is not labeled and may serve as a visual separator or placeholder. The chart uses distinct, saturated colors to differentiate categories and includes numerical labels directly on each slice for clarity.
